chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Jamil ibn Salih, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Verily, the Ziyarah (visitation) of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is equal to performing a Hajj with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) that is accepted (Mabrur).
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing the grave visitation of the Prophet as equivalent to a Hajj al-Mabrur performed in his direct company, a status that underscores the unique ontological rank of the Ahl al-Bayt in Shia theology. This comparison elevates Ziyarah from a mere commemorative act to a profound spiritual journey that mirrors the ultimate pilgrimage, reinforcing the continuity of prophetic guidance through the Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 19. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Jamīl ibn Sāliḥ, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, who said: Abū Ja’far (Imam Bāqir (a.s.)) said:
Verily (the reward for going to) the Ziyārah of the grave of the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) is equal to performing a purified Hajj with the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.).
